newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian gold miners owed $320 million for output.
newsitem.headline: Russian gold miners owed $320 million for output.

text.p: The Russian government owes gold miners 1.8 trillion roubles (about $320 million) for mined gold, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

The ministry's hard currency department, quoted by Interfax news agency, said it planned to send 2.8 trillion roubles to mining regions to finance output this year, with most of the financing to come in the form of promissory notes.

The head of the ministry's precious metals and stones department, Vladimir Rybkin, told Reuters that the ministry would hold a tender with commercial banks on Wednesday to borrow 2.8 trillion roubles to finance the gold sector.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits had said last week that the tender was scheduled for February 17.

Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov told Itar-Tass news agency earlier this month that Moscow planned to settle debts to the gold industry this month, but would finance no more than 30 percent of 1997 production.
Russian gold output in 1996 fell to around 110 tonnes from 122 tonnes in 1995, according to Industry Ministry figures in December 1996. Final official production figures have not yet been released.
